description: An introduction to cell division covering its importance, the basic cell cycle, mitosis and its role in growth and repair, meiosis and its role in producing gametes and variation, the differences between mitosis and meiosis, and the concepts of chromosomes, diploid and haploid cells.

mcq.questionText: What is meant by the term cell division?

options.text: The process by which a parent cell splits to form new daughter cells
The process by which a cell takes in food substances
The movement of materials in and out of a cell
The breaking down of glucose to release energy in a cell

mcq.explanation: Cell division is the process by which a parent cell divides to produce two or more daughter cells, allowing growth, repair and reproduction.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is an importance of cell division in living organisms?

options.text: It removes carbon dioxide from the body
It enables growth, repair and reproduction
It absorbs water through the roots
It changes light energy into chemical energy

mcq.explanation: Cell division increases the number of cells, allowing organisms to grow, replace worn-out or damaged cells, and reproduce.

mcq.questionText: Thread-like structures found in the nucleus that carry hereditary information are called:
mcq.explanation: Chromosomes are thread-like structures inside the nucleus that carry genes, which are the units of hereditary information.

mcq.questionText: A cell that contains two complete sets of chromosomes is described as:
mcq.explanation: A diploid cell has two sets of chromosomes (2n), one set inherited from each parent.

mcq.questionText: Which type of cell division produces two identical daughter cells used for growth and repair?
mcq.explanation: Mitosis produces two genetically identical daughter cells with the same chromosome number as the parent cell, and is responsible for growth and repair.

mcq.questionText: Which type of cell division produces gametes (sex cells)?
mcq.explanation: Meiosis is the type of cell division that produces gametes such as sperms and ova, each with half the chromosome number of the parent cell.

mcq.questionText: How many daughter cells are produced at the end of one complete meiotic division?
mcq.explanation: Meiosis involves two successive divisions, producing four haploid daughter cells from one parent cell.

mcq.questionText: During which stage of mitosis do the chromosomes line up along the middle (equator) of the cell?
mcq.explanation: In metaphase the chromosomes arrange themselves along the equator (middle) of the cell before being pulled apart.

mcq.questionText: During which stage of mitosis do the chromatids separate and move to opposite ends (poles) of the cell?
mcq.explanation: In anaphase the sister chromatids are pulled apart by spindle fibres and move towards opposite poles of the cell.

mcq.questionText: In which part of the cell cycle does a cell grow and copy (replicate) its DNA before dividing?
mcq.explanation: Interphase is the longest part of the cell cycle, during which the cell grows, carries out its functions and duplicates its DNA in preparation for division.

mcq.questionText: If a body cell of an organism has 24 chromosomes, how many chromosomes will each of its gametes contain?
mcq.explanation: Gametes are haploid and contain half the chromosome number of body cells, so 24 divided by 2 equals 12 chromosomes.

mcq.questionText: Why is meiosis important in living organisms that reproduce sexually?

options.text: It keeps the chromosome number constant from generation to generation and introduces variation
It produces cells that are exactly identical for repairing wounds
It increases the number of body cells during growth
It doubles the chromosome number in every gamete

mcq.explanation: Meiosis halves the chromosome number in gametes so that the normal number is restored at fertilisation, and it shuffles genes to create variation among offspring.

mcq.questionText: The division of the cytoplasm to complete the formation of two separate daughter cells is known as:
mcq.explanation: Cytokinesis is the division of the cytoplasm that follows nuclear division, separating the cell into two daughter cells.

mcq.questionText: Which statement best explains why daughter cells produced by mitosis are genetically identical to the parent cell?

options.text: Because the DNA is copied exactly before division and each daughter cell receives one full copy
Because the chromosome number is halved during the division
Because genes are exchanged between chromosomes during the division
Because four daughter cells share the chromosomes equally

mcq.explanation: Before mitosis the DNA is replicated exactly, so each daughter cell receives an identical and complete set of chromosomes.

mcq.questionText: In humans, where in the body does meiosis normally take place?

options.text: In the skin and bone marrow
In the reproductive organs (testes and ovaries)

mcq.explanation: Meiosis occurs in the reproductive organs, that is the testes and ovaries, where gametes (sperms and ova) are produced.

fib.questionText: The type of cell division that produces two identical daughter cells is called _____.
fib.explanation: Mitosis produces two genetically identical daughter cells with the same chromosome number as the parent.

fib.questionText: The type of cell division that produces gametes is called _____.
fib.explanation: Meiosis produces four haploid gametes, each with half the chromosome number of the parent cell.

fib.questionText: Thread-like structures in the nucleus that carry genes are called _____.
fib.explanation: Chromosomes carry the genes that determine the inherited characteristics of an organism.

fib.questionText: A cell that contains a single set of chromosomes is described as _____.
fib.explanation: A haploid cell (n), such as a gamete, contains only one set of chromosomes.

fib.questionText: A cell that contains two complete sets of chromosomes is described as _____.
fib.explanation: A diploid cell (2n) contains two sets of chromosomes, one from each parent.

fib.questionText: The stage of mitosis in which chromosomes line up at the equator of the cell is called _____.
fib.explanation: During metaphase the chromosomes arrange themselves along the middle of the cell.

fib.questionText: The part of the cell cycle during which the cell grows and copies its DNA is called _____.
fib.explanation: Interphase is the resting stage where the cell grows and duplicates its DNA before division begins.

fib.questionText: The division of the cytoplasm at the end of cell division is known as _____.
fib.explanation: Cytokinesis splits the cytoplasm so that two separate daughter cells are formed.

fib.questionText: The first stage of mitosis, in which chromosomes become visible as the nuclear membrane breaks down, is called _____.
fib.explanation: In prophase the chromosomes condense and become visible while the nuclear membrane disappears.

fib.questionText: Sex cells such as sperms and ova are also generally called _____.
fib.explanation: Gametes are the haploid sex cells that join during fertilisation to form a zygote.

tf.questionText: Mitosis produces two daughter cells that are genetically identical to the parent cell.
tf.explanation: Mitosis produces two daughter cells with exactly the same chromosomes as the parent cell.

tf.questionText: Meiosis produces four daughter cells, each with the same number of chromosomes as the parent cell.
tf.explanation: Meiosis produces four haploid cells, each with half the chromosome number of the parent cell.

tf.questionText: A diploid cell contains two sets of chromosomes.
tf.explanation: Diploid cells (2n) carry two sets of chromosomes, one set inherited from each parent.
Gametes are haploid cells, containing only one set of chromosomes.

tf.questionText: Cell division is important for growth and the repair of damaged tissues.
tf.explanation: By increasing cell numbers, cell division enables organisms to grow and to replace worn-out or injured cells.

tf.questionText: Meiosis is responsible for repairing wounds and healing the skin.
tf.explanation: Mitosis, not meiosis, is responsible for growth and the repair of damaged tissues.

tf.questionText: DNA is copied during interphase, before the cell begins to divide.
tf.explanation: During interphase the cell duplicates its DNA so that each daughter cell can receive a complete set.

tf.questionText: Meiosis introduces variation among the offspring of organisms that reproduce sexually.
tf.explanation: Meiosis shuffles and recombines genes, producing gametes that lead to genetically varied offspring.

tf.questionText: In mitosis the chromosome number of the daughter cells is half that of the parent cell.
tf.explanation: In mitosis the daughter cells keep the same chromosome number as the parent cell; it is meiosis that halves the number.

tf.questionText: Chromosomes are found inside the nucleus of a cell.
tf.explanation: Chromosomes are located within the nucleus and carry the hereditary material of the cell.

summary.correctAnswer: The process by which a parent cell divides to form new daughter cells.
summary.explanation: It allows organisms to grow, repair tissues and reproduce.

summary.correctAnswer: It enables growth, repair of tissues and reproduction.
summary.explanation: More cells mean increased body size, replacement of damaged cells and formation of new individuals.

summary.correctAnswer: Produces two identical daughter cells for growth and repair.
summary.explanation: The daughter cells have the same chromosome number as the parent.

summary.correctAnswer: Produces four haploid gametes and introduces variation.
summary.explanation: It halves the chromosome number so it is restored at fertilisation.

summary.correctAnswer: A cell having two sets of chromosomes (2n).
summary.explanation: One set comes from each parent, as in body cells.

summary.correctAnswer: A cell having one set of chromosomes (n).
summary.explanation: Gametes such as sperms and ova are haploid.
These four stages follow interphase to divide the nucleus.

summary.questionText: Role of interphase in the cell cycle
summary.correctAnswer: The cell grows and copies its DNA before dividing.
summary.explanation: It is the longest stage and prepares the cell for division.

summary.correctAnswer: Thread-like structures in the nucleus that carry genes.
summary.explanation: They pass on hereditary information from parents to offspring.

summary.questionText: Main difference between mitosis and meiosis
summary.correctAnswer: Mitosis keeps the chromosome number constant; meiosis halves it.
summary.explanation: Mitosis gives two identical cells while meiosis gives four varied haploid cells.

hoq.questionText: A scientist observes a dividing cell and counts 40 chromosomes lined up at the equator, then sees them split so that 40 chromatids move to each pole. The two new cells each end up with 40 chromosomes. What type of division is this and why?

options.text: Meiosis, because the chromosome number is halved
Mitosis, because the daughter cells keep the same chromosome number as the parent
Meiosis, because four cells are formed at the end
Fertilisation, because two cells join into one

hoq.explanation: Each daughter cell ends up with the same chromosome number (40) as the parent, which is the characteristic outcome of mitosis.

hoq.questionText: In a certain animal the body cells have 16 chromosomes. After a male gamete fertilises a female gamete, the zygote also has 16 chromosomes. Which process ensures that the zygote does NOT end up with 32 chromosomes?

options.text: Meiosis during the formation of gametes

hoq.explanation: Meiosis halves the chromosome number to 8 in each gamete, so that when two gametes fuse the original diploid number of 16 is restored.

hoq.questionText: Two offspring produced by mitosis from a single parent cell are always identical, but two offspring from sexual reproduction usually differ. Which combination of processes best explains this difference?

options.text: Mitosis copies DNA exactly, while meiosis and fertilisation reshuffle and combine genes to create variation
Mitosis halves the chromosomes, while meiosis keeps them the same
Both mitosis and meiosis always produce identical cells
Fertilisation removes half of the genes, causing differences

hoq.explanation: Mitosis copies DNA exactly to give identical cells, whereas meiosis reshuffles genes and fertilisation combines genes from two parents, producing varied offspring.
